title: Tough, Balanced and Inverted stay on in an interaction with a Pure card, against Pure's printed "ignore all other attributes"
summary: R289 (and R61, as R289 reads it) keep the stat attributes Tough, Balanced and Inverted applying in a Pure pairing because "they are stat layers". Pure's printed reminder ignores all other attributes, and the Manual lists Tough as an attribute. Under the authority order the printed text wins (rule attr.general.pure; D-U19-2). Suspected engine behaviour: a Pure blocker facing a Tough unit is priced against the doubled defense. Measured by the round-1 verifier: a Pure source dealing 5 to Rampart Guardian leaves it alive as a Tough 0/8. Measured by the round-2 verifier: a Balanced 4/1 dealt 3 by a Pure source survives as a 4/4.

title: The combat Unaware collapse is said to survive Pure, while noncombat Pure switches Unaware off
summary: R106 says the Unaware collapse of a combat exchange "survives {Pure}", because Unaware is a stat layer. R289 switches a Pure pairing's Unaware off outside combat, and Pure's printed reminder ignores all other attributes. The engine therefore appears to treat Unaware + Pure differently in combat and outside it, and the combat half contradicts the printed text (rule attr.general.pure; D-U19-2).

title: The engine balances a printed-Balanced unit before doubling an augment's Tough, against Manual p.42
summary: Manual p.42: Tough augmented onto a Balanced unit has its defense doubled, then its stats balanced. The engine follows R19's engine call (own printed attributes first, then augment-granted ones), so it balances first. Measured by the round-1 verifier: Child of Aether (printed Balanced, 2/0) augmented with Rampart Guardian (Tough) is a 2/4; the Manual makes it a 2/2. R19's premise that the Manual does not specify printed-vs-granted order is wrong for this pair. No test guards the printed-host case (rule attr.general.application-order; D-U19-1).
